mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real GDP growth above 3% for two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) when GDP growth exceeds 3% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5% combined with a concurrent rise in average hourly earnings signals tight labor markets, which increases input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in the industrial production index below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during six consecutive months of INDPRO contraction relative to its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts below 1 million units signals a collapse in residential construction demand, which negatively impacts homebuilding and related sectors, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when HOUST falls below 1,000,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their 12-month averages indicates a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the civilian labor force participation rate above 67% for four consecutive months signals broader labor market re-entry, which initially boosts aggregate demand but eventually increases wage pressure, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE not seasonally adjusted, civilian labor force participation rate > 67% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) when labor force participation remains above 67% for four consecutive months in a post-recession recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months indicates households are depleting savings buffers, which reduces discretionary spending power and depresses consumer-facing equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during eight consecutive months of RSAFS contraction relative to its 12-month moving average.
